findings.text: Idler axle: two ~1.7 mm rods taped together, held at one end ~140 mm from its bracket: belt tension bends and tilts them, so the belt walks
Idler position set by a row of holes: tension only in 6 mm steps, no lock, no squaring
Motor and idler each located from a different post with spacers: nothing puts both pulleys and the clamp in one plane
The motor pulley has one flange, and the two pulleys sit at different heights, so the runs slope
Belt link: hollow ladder bar and a hex key through a slot. No teeth engaged: it slips and has backlash
Pivot over the middle of the cart: a pendulum there hangs inside the frame, cannot pass the plate or rails, so it cannot swing up
No shaft, hub, arm or angle-sensor mount yet
One limit switch on a separate arm; no hard stops: the SC8UU blocks run into the SK8 supports
Electronics and leads loose on the desk; no strain relief on the moving cart
